newsitem.title: UK: Arson seen cause of Eurotunnel fire - source.
newsitem.headline: Arson seen cause of Eurotunnel fire - source.

text.p: Arson is now seen as the mostly likely cause of last November's Channel Tunnel fire, which caused 200 million pounds ($326.7 million) in damage, sources close to the British side of the investigation told Reuters Friday.
The French inquiry into the cause of the fire is due to give its findings in a press conference next week and British investigating officials believe arson will be named as the cause.

"We've heard through unofficial channels that once the report is published, it will clearly indicate a human cause -- arson," said a source within one of the British organisations that have been involved in the wider investigation.
He added, "We have not heard in a formal capacity but on the (fire) site visits the buzzword has been that it was arson."
Thursday evening the BBC ran a report saying the French judicial inquiry was expected to report that arson was the cause of the blaze, which to the hospitalization of truck drivers on Nov. 18.

The report's authors believed the fire was started deliberately. There has been some suggestion that the fire was the work of a disgruntled Eurotunnel worker or a truck driver. But none of these theories has been given any credence so far.
Earlier this week, the Channel Tunnel Safety Authority published its report into the blaze and slammed Eurotunnel, the operator, for fundamental failures in safety management.
It did not demand a redesign of the controversial open-sided freight wagons but did ask for tighter safety procedures.

The remaining key event for Eurotunnel, apart from next week's verdict on the cause of fire, is the decision from the Intergovernmental Commission on when Eurotunnel can resume freight traffic and what conditions are attached. That is also expected next week.
